title: iPhone 15 screen replacement
diagnosis: Your display glass is cracked, so we'll replace the whole display assembly. This is a hard repair for a first-timer, so go slowly and take your time.
safety_notes: Power off the phone before opening it.
Wear safety glasses and tape over badly cracked glass to avoid cuts.
Never puncture or bend the battery; stop if it looks swollen.

steps.title: Power off and prep
steps.instruction: Hold the side button and a volume button, then slide to power off. Unplug any cable and put clear tape over the cracked glass.
steps.expected_visual_state: The screen is black, no cable is attached, and clear tape covers the cracks.
common_mistakes: Skipping power off, which risks a short
Leaving cracked glass untaped so shards fall out

steps.title: Remove bottom screws
steps.instruction: Use the P2 pentalobe screwdriver to remove the two screws beside the USB-C port. Put them in a tray.
steps.expected_visual_state: Two small screws sit in a tray and the screw holes next to the USB-C port are empty.
common_mistakes: Using the wrong screwdriver and stripping the heads

steps.title: Soften the adhesive and lift the display
steps.instruction: Warm the edges of the screen with a heat pad, then attach the suction handle and pull gently to open a small gap. Slide the plastic spudger into the gap.
steps.expected_visual_state: A thin gap is visible between the display and the frame with a spudger inside it.
common_mistakes: Pulling too hard and cracking the screen more
Inserting the spudger deep and damaging internals

steps.title: Open the phone like a book
steps.instruction: Slide the spudger around the edges to release the adhesive. Swing the display open gently to the side, without pulling it far.
steps.expected_visual_state: The display is lifted and hinged open, with the ribbon cables still attached and the inside of the phone visible.
common_mistakes: Opening the display too far and tearing the cables
Pushing the spudger in too deep around the edges

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.instruction: Unscrew the battery bracket with the Phillips screwdriver and lift the battery connector with the spudger. Do this before touching any other connector.
steps.expected_visual_state: The battery bracket is removed and the battery connector is lifted free of its socket.
common_mistakes: Skipping this and risking a short circuit

steps.title: Remove the old display
steps.instruction: Unscrew the display bracket and unplug the display connectors with the spudger. Lift the old display away.
steps.expected_visual_state: The old display is fully detached and lying beside the phone, and the connector sockets are visible and empty.
common_mistakes: Pulling cables instead of lifting the connectors straight up

steps.title: Connect the new display
steps.instruction: Plug in the new display connectors and refit the display bracket. Then reconnect the battery.
steps.expected_visual_state: The new display is connected with the bracket screwed down and the battery connector clicked in.
common_mistakes: Connectors not fully aligned or seated
Reconnecting the battery before checking the display connectors

steps.title: Close up and test
steps.instruction: Press the display onto the frame, replace the bottom screws, and power on. Check touch response across the whole screen.
steps.expected_visual_state: The phone shows the Apple logo and then a clear, uncracked display that responds to touch everywhere.
common_mistakes: Closing the phone with a cable trapped under the display
Not testing touch in the screen corners
